To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the absence of a stimulus (e.g., ovulation) the oxygen tension of the ovidutal fluid is very low, and that at the time of ovulaton, the presence of an oocyte or of the oviducal probe increases the oxygen tension in a similar fashion.

in the absence of a fertilized ovum the oxygen tension in oviductal tubal fluid is very low and that the presence of a fertilized ova in the oviducal tubal fluid increases the oxygen tension in tubal fluid.
the oxygen tension in oviductal fluids of rhesus monkeys is very low, less then 10 Torr, and that at and shortly after ovula- tion, the oxygen tension increases to a value of approximately 60 Torr.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxygenation of the rhesous monkey oviduct and its relation to ovulation.
the role of oxygen tension in the fertilization of the human oviduct.
the role of oxygen tension in the survival and development of the oviducal egg and embryo in the rhesus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ovum and the oviduct are not independent of each other but are interdependent in their oxygen requirements and that the oxygen supply to the oviduct is controlled by a feedback mechanism.
, in the monkey, the oxygen concentration in the oviducal fluid is very low in the follicular phase of the cycle.

the oxygen tension in oviductal tubal fluid is very low, but that at ovulation and shortly thereafter it increases to the same level as in the blood and that this increase is a result of the presence of a foreign body (oocyte or probe) in the tube.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ovulation is accompanied by an increased oxygen tension in the fluid of the oviductive tract which is essential for fertilization.

the ovum is the stimulus which provides a suitable environment for fertilization and early embryonic development in the oviducal fluid, and that the ovum does this by providing the stimulus for a local increase in the oxygen content of the oviducat fluid.
the oviduct has a very low oxygen tension in the follicular phase and that at ovulation, the oxygen tension is increased by a mechanism which is not yet understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxygen plays an important role in the fertilization process and the development of the embryo.
the oxygen supply in the tube is not constant but changes in relation to ovulation.
the oviduct is not a passive structure, but rather it actively participates in gamete survival, gamete transport, and early embryogenesis.
